question: Step B: do SV's stock picks improve a proven portfolio? SV takes 0, 20, 35 or 50% of the account (5% per stock, up to 0, 4, 7 or 10 stocks), the rest sits in the core (the Permanent Portfolio, with All Weather as a check) and 5% is always kept in cash.

PERM.label: Permanent Portfolio: stocks, long bonds, gold, cash 25% each

AW.label: All Weather: 30% stocks, 55% bonds, 15% gold and commodities
AW.source: Ray Dalio (as published by Tony Robbins, 2014)

variants.label: SV picks alone, step 1 setting (5% per stock, up to 10), rest in cash

selection.rule: SV is added only if a satellite beats the Permanent core without SV on both Sharpe and Calmar with a worst fall within 25%; within 0.01 Sharpe the smaller satellite wins; the same share is reported on All Weather.

next_step: If SV is added: sector limits on the satellite (step 2), then the forward test and practice account. If not: the core alone goes forward, and SV research returns to what it buys (entries and signal quality) before trying again.
notes: Core + satellite as in Vanguard's model portfolios. The core is the proven portfolio chosen in c1-proven-portfolios-v1 (Permanent Portfolio), with All Weather as a robustness check because gold's strong run flatters both.

Each SV stock is 5% of the account (risk 0.5% at the stop, total open risk 10%), the step 1 choice; buying a stock sells that much of the core and a sale buys it back, 0.1% per side on each move. The 5% cash reserve (in SHY, short-term Treasuries) is reset at each month end.
Same signals, selling rule (current stop, no 2R target, 40 days) and luck check as before; window 2007-01-03 to 2026-01-16 like the proven-portfolio test; signals before 2007 are not traded.
Deflated Sharpe counts 71 trials: 62 SV account tests on this signal set plus these 9.
